hints: When is it impossible? Think about a letter that appears more than half the time. Then, to get the alphabetically smallest answer, decide the string one position at a time.

A multiset of letters with m positions left can be arranged iff no letter appears more than ⌈m/2⌉ times. Build greedily: at each position try letters a→z and take the first that differs from the previous letter and leaves a feasible remainder.

1. Count letters; if any count > ⌈n/2⌉ return "".
  2. For each position, with m = positions left after this one:
  3. Try letters in order, skipping zero counts and the previous letter.
  4. Tentatively use it; it is safe if its own count ≤ ⌊m/2⌋ (it cannot start the rest) and every count ≤ ⌈m/2⌉.
  5. Keep the first safe letter and move on.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Generate all distinct permutations in sorted order and return the first with no equal neighbours.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Greedy smallest-letter choice at each position with an O(26) feasibility check on the remaining counts.

explain: For "aabbc" (a2, b2, c1): position 1 tries a; remaining a1 b2 c1 over 4 slots is fine, so take a. Position 2 skips a and takes b. Position 3 takes a, position 4 skips a (used up) and takes b, and the last is c, giving "ababc". The used letter's limit is ⌊m/2⌋ because the next position cannot repeat it. For "kkkx", k appears 3 > ⌈4/2⌉ times, so the answer is "".
recognize: 'No two adjacent equal' plus 'rearrange' → frequency counts with a max-count feasibility rule (heap greedy, here made lexicographic).
